proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 and H^m(M ∖ V) = 0; consequently H^m-a.e. x ∈ M has its approximate tangent plane T_x contained in V, so Λ_m q ξ(x) = ξ(x) for μ_T-a.e. x"). This is the identity q_#T = T behind Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2 (chapter-07.txt lines 358–362).
Approximate tangent spaces follow Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86), in SimonGMT's form. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q means: dim Q = m, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) (blowUpMap).
1. (H^m(M ∖ V) = 0.) The set ℝ^P ∖ V is open, because the finite-dimensional subspace V is closed. Hence μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = ∫⁻_{ℝ^P∖V} θ d(H^m⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M∖V} θ dH^m (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). θ is ℕ-valued and θ > 0 on M (mult_pos), so θ ≥ 1 on M. Therefore H^m(M ∖ V) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∖V} θ dH^m = μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0.
2. (Good set.) Let G be the set of x ∈ M ∩ V for which some subspace Q satisfies both HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. R.orients holds for H^m⌞M-a.e. x, and step 1 gives H^m(M ∖ V) = 0. So H^m⌞M-almost every x lies in G.
3. (Tangent planes lie in V.) Let x ∈ G with its subspace Q; we show Q ⊆ V. If m = 0 then dim Q = 0, so Q = {0} ⊆ V. Let m ≥ 1 and suppose some v ∈ Q ∖ V. Since V is closed, δ := dist(v, V) > 0. Define f(y) := max(0, δ/2 − ‖y − v‖). Then f is continuous, f ≥ 0, f(v) = δ/2, and f vanishes outside the compact ball B̄(v, δ/2), so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Also f(y) = 0 for y ∈ V, because ‖y − v‖ ≥ δ there.
 (a) For every r > 0, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^m = 0. Let y = η_{x,r}(z) with z ∈ M and y ∉ V. Then z ∉ V, since x ∈ V gives η_{x,r}(z) = r^{-1}(z − x) ∈ V whenever z ∈ V. Hence {y ∈ η_{x,r}(M) : f(y) ≠ 0} ⊆ η_{x,r}(M) ∖ V ⊆ η_{x,r}(M ∖ V). The map η_{x,r} is Lipschitz with constant r^{-1} and H^m(M ∖ V) = 0, so H^m(η_{x,r}(M ∖ V)) = 0. (Lipschitz images of H^m-null sets are H^m-null: Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, and μHE[m] is a positive multiple of μH[m].) The set {f ≠ 0} is open, hence measurable. So its measure for H^m restricted to η_{x,r}(M) is H^m({f ≠ 0} ∩ η_{x,r}(M)) = 0, f = 0 almost everywhere for that restricted measure, and the integral is 0.
 (b) Apply HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q to f: ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0. By (a), ∫_Q f dH^m = 0.
 (c) dim Q = m. Choose an orthonormal basis of Q and the corresponding linear isometry ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P (Euclid m → Euclid P) with range Q. μHE is preserved by isometries (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure / Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and μHE[m] on ℝ^m is Lebesgue measure L^m. Hence ∫_Q f dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} f(ιz) dL^m(z). Put z₀ := ι^{-1}(v). If ‖z − z₀‖ < δ/4 then ‖ιz − v‖ < δ/4, so f(ιz) > δ/4. Therefore ∫_Q f dH^m ≥ (δ/4)·L^m(B(z₀, δ/4)) > 0, which contradicts (b). So Q ⊆ V.
4. (Pointwise identity on G.) Let x ∈ G with Q as above. By IsUnitOrientationOf choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) spanning Q and ε ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(β) = ε·β(τ) for all m-covectors β. Since x ∈ V and every τ_i ∈ Q ⊆ V, we have qx = x and qτ_i = τ_i (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). So q^#ω(x) = ω(0 + qx)∘Λ^m q = ω(x)∘Λ^m q, and ξ(x)(q^#ω(x)) = ε·ω(x)(qτ_1, …, qτ_m) = ε·ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_m) = ξ(x)(ω(x)).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 4, θ(x)·ξ(x)(q^#ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) for H^m⌞M-a.e. x. Functions that agree almost everywhere have the same Bochner integral, with no integrability needed (Mathlib integral_congr_ae for μHE[m].restrict M). Therefore R.action(q^#ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(q^#ω) dH^m = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH^m = R.action(ω). ∎
key_steps: μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 and θ ≥ 1 on M give H^m(M ∖ V) = 0.
At H^m-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ V an approximate tangent plane Q exists and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q.
Q ⊆ V: a C_c bump vanishing on V has zero blow-up integrals over η_{x,r}(M), but it would have positive integral over Q if Q ⊄ V.
q is the identity on V ⊇ Q, so ξ(x)(q^#ω(x)) = ξ(x)(ω(x)) a.e. on M; integrate.
